Still open — this is the live scientific frontier. conversion_ceiling_root: 6 hypotheses, 4 alive (H-substrate-ceiling, H-f-dominance, H-objective-misspecification, H-observation-interface), 2 eliminated, 0 confirmed, decidable: false. Where the two overlap

2 named cases this cycle — and 1 deliberate non-case

conversion_ceiling_root / e3_fdominance_causal_discrimination · hard problem plus an empty queue

REE-side (hard, not addressable by process): 8 alive hypotheses across the two spaces, 0 confirmed on the root question, both marked decidable: false. V3-EXQ-925 discovered an H0 selector-regime confound that must be controlled before H1–H4 can be discriminated at all. This is genuinely complex (probe-gated).

REE_assembly-side (addressable): both spaces carry an explicitly pre-registered live gate — the return-decomposition diagnostic, and the regime-matched re-test — and neither is queued, while the queue has sat empty for 34 hours. The science is waiting on an experiment that has already been specified. That gap is throughput, not difficulty.

The distinction matters for how this gets reported: the ceiling’s 26 failure records look like a substrate wall, but the immediate blocker is an unqueued, already-designed diagnostic.

INV-050 / MECH-180 (EXQ-861) · hard problem plus a governance defect that cost a run

REE-side (hard): 9 iterations to reach a PASS, and the underlying space still holds 2 alive hypotheses (H1 vs H3 on the 861e seed-271 collapse). The 2026-08-23 autopsy adopted H3 as a substrate/machine delta and explicitly declined to treat it as ledger-confirmed.

REE_assembly-side (addressable): 861f ran twice — two manifests, two DB rows, both PASS — because a stale TASK_CLAIMS entry was reaped mid-run (chip-20260824-exq861f-duplicate-run-stale-claim-reap). On a chain that already needed 9 iterations, the apparatus spent a tenth reproducing the ninth. Pure process cost, on the most iteration-expensive chain in the window.

Explicitly NOT an overlap case · SD-017 / ARC-045 / MECH-166 (EXQ-436)

This chain has the weakest confidence movement per run of any here — 5 FAILs, 1 alive hypothesis, 0 resolved — but it is among the best-served nodes on the REE_assembly side: 62 autopsies name it, it carries a done task claim, and it has 2–3 commits in the last 7 days. Its slowness is entirely REE-side. Reading it as a process problem would be the exact error this split exists to prevent.
